A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAD study and provide readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered supplementary material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original concept-erasure and amplification experiments, adversarial-prompt evaluations, and supplementary Stable Diffusion 2.1 results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds module-specific pruning results and non-target-class measurements for amplification.

M1.justification: The weight-times-gradient attribution approximation, editing objectives, and positive/negative top-k pruning procedures remain unchanged. CAD-Erase and CAD-Amplify name the existing algorithms; the module comparisons are ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ImageNette objects, I2P prompts, COCO preservation prompts, five artist styles, and adversarial-prompt scenarios. The new module study uses the existing object task; supplementary Stable Diffusion 2.1 experiments were already present.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their baseline membership: ConceptPrune, ESD, RECE, and UCE for SD-1.4 object/nudity erasure; ESD, RECE, and UCE for style LPIPS; and RECE/UCE for SD-2.1. UnlearnDiffAtk is shortened to UnlearnDiff. New module variants are CAD ablation conditions.

E3.justification: New Appendix Section 10 compares pruning restricted to feed-forward, self-attention, cross-attention, and residual modules. Existing benchmark sample counts, pruning ratios, and Appendix Section 9 settings are retained. Naming Nudenet 3.4.2 does not establish a detector-version change from v1.

E4.justification: V2 adds a systematic four-module ablation across ten object classes (Table 8), testing how pruning location affects erasure and collateral damage. Table 6 also adds non-target-class evaluation during amplification. These substantially extend the analyses beyond the retained ratio sensitivity, approximation validation, and adversarial tests.

E5.justification: Both versions specify benchmark seed 0 and 1,000 random-mask trials for approximation validation. Neither adds repeated-seed summaries, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 3 substantially revises adversarial-prompt counts and rankings: Ring-a-bell RECE changes from 97 to 4 and ConceptPrune from 13 to 83, while CAD remains at 5. Table 6 adds other-class amplification accuracies, and new Table 8 reports module-dependent outcomes. These are revised or additional reports; the unexplained count revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The masking formulation, linear approximation, first-order derivation, editing objectives, and two hypotheses are retained. V2 makes concept and parameter dependencies explicit in notation but introduces no substantive mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain efficient component attribution, localized positive parameters, negative components that suppress concepts, and editing through their removal. V2 reorganizes these contributions and emphasizes the named inference-time editing algorithms without materially changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix Section 10 interprets the greater collateral damage from attention and residual pruning as stronger concept entanglement outside feed-forward layers. Existing limitations concerning shared knowledge, parameter-level analysis, and potentially better editing strategies remain.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly identifies the evaluator as Nudenet 3.4.2. Appendix Section 9 retains its hyperparameters, batch sizes, A5000 hardware, and checkpoint information. The shortened code-link text points to the same repository.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through input-attribution methods, gradient-based pruning, and diffusion weight-space interpretation, explaining their differences from CAD. Existing comparisons with Cones and knowledge amplification move from Section 7 into related work; those passages are not new contributions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, related work is reorganized and expanded, and the method exposition gains clearer subheadings and explicit dependencies. CAD-Erase/CAD-Amplify terminology is propagated throughout, while Section 7 becomes a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 8, expands Table 6, compresses Table 4 to one column, and relocates several figures and tables. Figure 7 is cropped, resized, and moved with identical plotted data. The qualitative image panels are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 6 now exposes amplification's collateral effects, and Appendix Table 8 clarifies how pruning location affects erasure and preservation. Rewritten explanations and broader related work improve clarity and positioning. These provide a useful overall gain, although the unexplained revisions to Table 3 limit improvement in evidential transparency.
